slide_title:
Gradient Descent (GD) – Stochastic Gradient Descent SGD)
and Mini-Batch Gradient Descent

bullets: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a variant of GD which computes the gradient of the Error function with respect to a single training example
In other words, it updates the weights using one training sample at a time
Remember: GD updated the weight vector after passing through ALL training samples.
SGD is usually more efficient than GD
labels: Batch GD is a generalization of GD and SGD where weights are updated after passing through “Mini-Batch” of training samples with size n
If n=N (it is GD), and if n=1 (it is SGD)

Inside it, place three bullets with blue arrow markers: 'Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a variant of GD which computes the gradient of the Error function with respect to a single training example'; 'In other words, it updates the weights using one training sample at a time'; 'Remember: GD updated the weight vector after passing through ALL training samples.' 6. Below the equation, still inside the blue-bordered panel, add bold red #C00000 subheading 'Why using SGD', then two bullets: 'SGD is usually more efficient than GD' with 'efficient' in red, and 'SGD converges faster than GD'. 8. Below the panel, add bold red #C00000 text: 'Batch GD is a generalization of GD and SGD where weights are updated after passing through “Mini-Batch” of training samples with size n'. 9. Under that, add centered bold blue #0000FF text: 'If n=N (it is GD), and if n=1 (it is SGD)'. 10. Do not add the red mouse pointer unless intentionally reproducing the screenshot cursor.
